mainPoints.explanation: The tool provides a complete pipeline from reading articles → selecting paragraphs → categorizing → conceptualizing → checking, offering far more control than standalone image generation and ensuring illustration quality and consistency.
mainPoints.point: Open-sources a standardized AI illustration skill where the core is workflow rather than single-image generation capability.

mainPoints.explanation: Users can pick characters to use directly or substitute their own IP; multiple art style skins can switch according to article tone while core features remain unchanged, maintaining recognizability.
mainPoints.point: 31 ready-made original characters lower the barrier to entry, with support for changing skins without changing characters.

mainPoints.explanation: Based on the author's experience, these character design principles emphasize shaping IP through minimal forms and emotional resonance rather than piling on stylistic details.
mainPoints.point: Proposes three IP laws: 'weak persona / contrast > strong styling,' 'characters are emotional synonyms,' and 'distinctiveness lies in posture and attitude.'

mainPoints.explanation: Paragraph-by-paragraph review (no skipping), categorized illustration (emotion/explanation/comic), categorize before drawing, and post-drawing self-check — these rules improve the match between illustrations and content.
mainPoints.point: The illustration decision workflow is solidified into four hard rules to prevent AI from cutting corners or going off track.

oneSentenceSummary: The author open-sources their daily AI illustration workflow "Xiao Hu IP Studio," featuring 31 original characters, multiple art style skins, and a systematic illustration methodology that enables AI to read articles, plan visuals, and generate consistent illustrations automatically.
originalTitle: 我把自己的 IP 配图技能开源了 顺手做了 31 个现成角色
summary: The article details the author's open-source project "Xiao Hu IP Studio" — an Agent Skill-based AI illustration tool. Key highlights include: 31 original characters in a unified hand-drawn style (15 workplace personas + 16 pun-based memes), allowing users to start immediately without building their own IP; multiple art style skins (blind box figurines, black-and-white line art, flat vector, watercolor, etc.) that adapt to article tone while preserving character recognizability; and a solidified illustration decision workflow — paragraph-by-paragraph review, categorized illustration, and self-check rework — ensuring every image precisely serves its content. The author also shares the "Three IP Laws" and "Four Hard Rules" of character design, along with foolproof installation instructions (one sentence lets AI install itself), supporting tools like Claude Code and Codex. The article concludes with acknowledgments to inspiring predecessor projects (Xiao Hei, Baoyu, etc.) and is released under the MIT license.
title: I Open-Sourced My IP Illustration Skill and Built 31 Ready-to-Use Characters
